transcript.text: Hi everyone, I wanted to get us together to talk through the current draft plan for the Harbor Roof rooftop performance video. As it stands, the plan includes live amplified playback, a two-person aerial rig, a branded bar set, and ordinary editorial approval. I make the final call on whether the shoot plan is approved, but before I approve anything, I'll need us to go through the routine verbal signoff from the location, safety, and artist representatives at our final lock meeting. Let's start working through any concerns or adjustments we need to make.

This means we cannot use live amplified playback as currently planned — we'll need to switch to silent playback with the finished music added in post. I have the permit email in my location folder documenting this restriction.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical safety issue before we go any further. I completed my roof-anchor inspection this morning, and the certified anchor at Harbor Roof supports only one performer — not two. It also requires a fall-arrest harness for anyone using it, and explicitly prohibits pyrotechnics on the roof. This directly conflicts with the current plan's two-person aerial rig. We need to either reduce the aerial rig to a single performer or find an alternative rigging solution. I have not yet entered this in the production safety log, but I'm putting it on the table now so we can address it before any approval.

transcript.text: I need to flag two critical issues from the artist's side before we go any further. I received the countersigned rider from the artist's lawyer yesterday, and it contains two provisions that directly conflict with our current plan. First, the rider explicitly prohibits visible alcohol branding — which means the branded bar set in our current draft plan is a no-go. Second, the rider requires the artist to approve the final cut before release, which means our ordinary editorial approval process won't suffice — we'll need to add an artist approval step. I haven't uploaded the signed rider to the shared production file yet, but these are hard contractual requirements we need to address before any approval.
